examples.en: They gave me just a tiny taste, so it only makes me crave more.

examples.ko: 드라마가 일주일에 한 편만 나와서 감질났어요.
examples.en: The drama only airs one episode a week, so it left me wanting more.

examples.ko: 감질나게 조금씩 말하지 말고 다 이야기해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't tease me by telling it bit by bit. Tell me everything.

examples.ko: 샘플만 먹어 보니까 더 감질나는 거 있죠?
examples.en: Having tried only the sample, I'm craving more, you know?

examples.ko: 빵을 한 입만 먹었더니 감질나서 더 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: I only had one bite of the bread, so I'm left wanting more.
They told me to eat only a little, so it's unsatisfying, but I'll hold back.

explain: 조금만 맛보거나 조금만 해서 성에 차지 않고 오히려 더 하고 싶어질 때 써요. 음식뿐 아니라 드라마, 이야기, 소식처럼 조금씩만 주어지는 것에도 말해요. '감질나게 하다'처럼 남을 애태우는 말로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: They only reveal a bit, which teases people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 애태우며 더 궁금하게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for teasing someone and making them want more.

phrases.example: 한 입만 먹었더니 감질나서 더 먹고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I only had one bite, so now I want more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 연결형으로, 부족해서 더 하고 싶은 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective giving the reason: wanting more because it wasn't enough.

phrases.example: 감질나게 조금만 주지 말고 더 주세요.
phrases.en: Don't give me just a teasing little bit; give me more.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게' 형태로 쓰면 너무 조금이라 오히려 더 애가 탄다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-게' form conveys that it's so little it only makes you want more.

explain_en: Use it when you get only a little of something, so you are not satisfied and want more. It applies to food and also to dramas, stories or news that come out in small portions. '감질나게 하다' is also common for teasing someone.

examples.en: My friend often exaggerates stories.
Please don't exaggerate so much.
He overstated his skills.

examples.ko: 과장해서 말하면 하루 종일 기다린 것 같아요.
examples.en: If I exaggerate, it feels like I waited all day.
I'm uncomfortable around people who exaggerate.
You don't need to inflate your experience at an interview.

explain: '과장하다'는 하는 사람이 있는 말이에요. 같은 일을 '과장되다'로 쓰면 말한 사람보다 이야기가 어떻게 됐는지에 초점이 가요. '과장해서 말하다'가 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.

phrases.en: My friend often exaggerates when speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form.
phrases.en_equiv: to speak in an exaggerated way

phrases.en: I'll tell you without exaggerating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 있는 그대로 말하겠다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when promising to tell it as it is.

phrases.en: That person exaggerates a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과장을 자주 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who exaggerates often.

explain_en: 과장하다 has a person doing the exaggerating. With 과장되다 the focus moves from the speaker to what happened to the story. '과장해서 말하다' (to speak with exaggeration) is a common pattern.

en: to be welcome; to be satisfactory

examples.en: That news isn't very welcome to me.
An unwelcome guest suddenly came by.

examples.ko: 달가운 소식이 있으면 바로 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If you have welcome news, please tell me right away.
Even though it was kind, it didn't sound welcome to me.

examples.ko: 솔직히 그 제안이 달갑다고는 말 못 해요.
examples.en: Honestly, I can't say that proposal is welcome.

examples.ko: 달갑지는 않지만 어쩔 수 없이 받아들였어요.
examples.en: I didn't like it, but I had no choice but to accept.

explain: 거의 '달갑지 않다' 모양으로 써요. ㅂ 불규칙이라서 '달가워요, 달가운'으로 바뀌어요. '반갑다'가 기쁜 만남이나 소식에 쓴다면, 달갑다는 마음에 들고 내키는 느낌에 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 달갑지 않은 손님이 와서 기분이 안 좋아요.
phrases.en: An unwelcome guest came, so I'm in a bad mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오는 것이 반갑지 않은 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone whose arrival isn't welcome.

phrases.en: I heard unwelcome news at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣고 싶지 않은 소식을 말할 때 써요. '달갑다'는 거의 부정으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for news you don't want to hear; 달갑다 is almost always used in the negative.

phrases.en: My work suddenly increased, and I'm not happy about it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음에 들지 않을 때 쓰는 해요체 부정문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative sentence for when something isn't welcome.

explain_en: It almost always appears as '달갑지 않다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '달가워요' and '달가운'. While '반갑다' is for happy meetings or news, 달갑다 is about something that feels agreeable and appealing.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리는 동안 바늘방석에 앉은 기분이었어요.
examples.en: While waiting for my test results, I felt like I was sitting on pins and needles.
I sat next to my boss, so the whole meeting was agony.
My grandmother keeps her needles stuck in a pin cushion.

examples.ko: 다들 아는 사실을 나만 몰라서 바늘방석 같았어요.
examples.en: Everyone knew but me, so I felt awfully uncomfortable.
I don't know where I put the pin cushion.

examples.ko: 그 자리는 정말 바늘방석이라 얼른 나오고 싶었어요.
examples.en: That seat was so uncomfortable that I wanted to leave right away.

explain: 바늘을 꽂아 두는 물건이지만, 대화에서는 마음이 불편하고 불안한 자리를 비유할 때 더 많이 나와요. 보통 '바늘방석에 앉다, 바늘방석 같다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 면접 내내 바늘방석에 앉은 것처럼 불안했어요.
phrases.en: to feel very uneasy in a situation
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 앉는 것이 아니라 불안하고 불편한 상황에 있을 때 써요. '바늘방석에 앉은 기분'이라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: You are not literally sitting; it describes being in an anxious, uncomfortable situation. People also say '바늘방석에 앉은 기분'.
phrases.en_equiv: be on pins and needles; feel like squirming in one's seat

explain_en: It is literally a pin cushion, but in conversation it is often used figuratively for a seat or situation where you feel uneasy. It usually appears as '바늘방석에 앉다' or '바늘방석 같다'.

examples.en: What is the reason for your sudden change of heart?

examples.ko: 최근에 가장 이해가 안 가는 건 주인아주머니의 변심이에요.
examples.en: What I understand least lately is the landlady's change of heart.
The customer changed their mind and requested a refund.
You can't exchange it for a simple change of mind.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 변심을 알고 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: I was heartbroken to learn that person had had a change of heart.
I don't know why my friend changed their mind.

explain: 쇼핑몰의 '단순 변심 환불'처럼 마음이 바뀌었다는 뜻으로 많이 보여요. 연애나 약속에서 쓰면 '마음이 변하다'보다 배신당한 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 단순 변심으로도 일주일 안에 환불할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can get a refund within a week even for a simple change of mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑몰 환불 안내에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in online store refund notices.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 변심한 것 같아서 마음이 아파요.
phrases.en: I think his feelings for me have changed, and it hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변심'을 동사로 만든 말이에요. 사랑하는 마음이 변할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 변심, often used when feelings of love change.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a change of heart

phrases.en: I suddenly changed my mind and canceled the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변심'보다 일상에서 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요. 배신당한 느낌은 거의 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter everyday expression than 변심, with little sense of betrayal.

explain_en: You often see it in shopping-mall phrases like '단순 변심 환불' (refund for a simple change of mind). In romance or promises, it feels more like being betrayed than the plainer '마음이 변하다'.

examples.en: The main character takes revenge on the bad guy in the movie.
He said he would take revenge for his friend.
Will I feel at ease after taking revenge?
He prepared for a long time in order to get revenge.
In the drama, the person who took revenge ends up regretting it.
How about forgiving instead of taking revenge?

explain: '복수하다'는 드라마, 영화, 소설에 자주 나오는 말이고 일상에서는 장난으로 쓰기도 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '갚아 주다'나 '되갚다'가 비슷한 상황에 더 가볍게 쓰여요. 같은 소리의 '복수(여럿)'와 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 오랫동안 복수를 꿈꿔 왔어요.
phrases.en: He has dreamed of revenge for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '복수'를 써서 마음속 바람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 복수 to talk about a wish held inside.

phrases.example: 나쁜 일을 한 사람에게 되갚아 주고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to pay back the person who did something bad to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '복수하다'보다 가볍게 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter word than 복수하다 for everyday use.

phrases.en: I will take revenge for sure someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 하겠다는 강한 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state a strong intention for the future.

explain_en: 복수하다 is common in dramas, movies and novels, and people sometimes use it jokingly. In casual talk, 갚아 주다 or 되갚다 fits similar situations in a lighter way. Don't confuse it with another word 복수 that means 'plural'.

examples.ko: 친구가 상을 받았다고 샘내면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't be jealous just because your friend won a prize.

examples.ko: 동생은 제가 새 가방을 사면 늘 샘내요.
examples.en: My younger sibling always gets envious when I buy a new bag.
The way she was acting jealous was so cute that I laughed.
She was jealous because her older sister got praised.

examples.ko: 형이 용돈을 더 받는다고 샘내서 싸웠어요.
examples.en: He was jealous that his older brother got more allowance, so they fought.

examples.ko: 샘내지 않고 친구를 진심으로 축하해 줬어요.
examples.en: I congratulated my friend sincerely without feeling jealous.

explain: '샘이 나다'는 내 마음이 그렇다는 말이고, '샘내다'는 그 마음을 겉으로 드러낸다는 느낌이에요. '샘을 내다'처럼 띄어 써서 말하기도 해요. 형제나 친구처럼 가까운 사이의 가벼운 질투에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 동생이 제 새 가방을 보고 샘을 내요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling envies me when seeing my new bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '샘내다'를 띄어 쓴 말로, 뜻은 같고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of '샘내다' with the same meaning, often used in speech.

phrases.en: Don't be envious just because your friend did well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 질투하지 말라고 부드럽게 말릴 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to tell someone not to act envious.

phrases.example: 친구의 새 신발을 보니 샘이 나요.
phrases.en: I feel envious seeing my friend's new shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '샘내다'는 겉으로 드러내는 행동이고, '샘이 나다'는 마음속에서 드는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '샘이 나다' is the inner feeling, while '샘내다' is showing it outwardly.

explain_en: '샘이 나다' says that you feel envy, while '샘내다' feels like showing that envy outwardly. People also say it as '샘을 내다'. It suits light jealousy between close people such as siblings or friends.

en: to be uninterested; to be indisposed

examples.en: My younger sibling looked uninterested even after getting a present.
My friend answered my story half-heartedly.
Lately I feel indifferent about everything.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 기대했는데 보고 나니 심드렁했어요.
examples.en: I had high hopes for that movie, but I felt underwhelmed after watching it.
Why do you look so uninterested?
Even the game I played for a while has lost its appeal now.

explain: '시큰둥하다'와 비슷하게 써요. 관심이 없어 보이거나 반응이 시원치 않을 때 '심드렁한 표정', '심드렁하게 대답하다'처럼 사람의 표정, 대답, 태도에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling looks somehow listless today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여 겉모습에서 느껴지는 무관심을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아/어 보이다, it describes indifference that shows in someone's appearance.

phrases.en: The director was disappointed by the audience's lukewarm reaction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대한 만큼 호응이 없을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for when the response is less than expected.

phrases.en: Even though I made the suggestion, my friend was unenthusiastic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심드렁하다'와 비슷하고 마음에 안 드는 듯 반응이 시원치 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 심드렁하다, used when the response is lukewarm as if displeased.

explain_en: It is used much like '시큰둥하다'. When someone seems uninterested or reacts lukewarmly, it describes their expression, answer or attitude, as in '심드렁한 표정' or '심드렁하게 대답하다'.

examples.en: Aw, you left your umbrella behind again?
Aw, how hard it must be, having caught a cold.
Oh dear, how could you say it like that?
Oh my, you've already finished it all?
Ugh, you're going to be the death of me!

examples.ko: 에이그, 숙제도 안 하고 놀고만 있어요.
examples.en: Tsk, you're just playing without doing your homework.

explain: 못마땅하거나 안쓰럽거나 답답할 때 혼잣말처럼 나오는 소리예요. 상대에게 크게 화내기보다 한숨 섞인 아쉬움을 나타내고, 비슷한 상황에서 '아이고'도 써요.

phrases.en: Aw, what a waste. You threw all the food away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아쉬운 마음을 혼잣말처럼 말할 때 뒤에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Added as a sigh of regret, like talking to yourself.

phrases.en: Oh dear, what should I do? I lost my wallet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 답답하고 걱정스러운 마음이 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you feel frustrated and worried.
phrases.en_equiv: oh dear, what should I do

phrases.en: Oh my, that must really hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에이그'보다 걱정하고 안쓰러운 마음이 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds softer and more sympathetic than '에이그'.

explain_en: It is a sound that slips out like a mutter when you are displeased, sympathetic or exasperated. It expresses sighing disappointment rather than real anger at someone, and '아이고' can be used in similar situations.

en: not ordinary; extremely (used with a negative)

examples.ko: 이사 준비하느라 이만저만 고생한 게 아니에요.
examples.en: I went through no small trouble preparing for the move.

examples.ko: 아들이 시험에 떨어져서 어머니의 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요.
examples.en: Her son failed the exam, so the mother's worry is no small matter.

examples.ko: 오늘 일이 이만저만 바쁜 게 아니에요.
examples.en: Work today is extremely busy.

examples.ko: 비가 이만저만 오는 게 아니라서 우산도 소용없어요.
examples.en: It's raining so hard that even an umbrella is useless.

examples.ko: 아이를 혼자 키우는 일은 이만저만 부담이 아니에요.
examples.en: Raising a child alone is a very heavy burden.
The heat this summer was something else.

explain: 거의 항상 '이만저만이 아니다', '이만저만 ~(으)ㄴ 게 아니다'처럼 부정문에서 써요. '이만저만 바빠요'처럼 긍정문으로 쓰면 어색해요. 부정 표현이 붙어도 뜻은 반대로 '정도가 아주 심하다'예요. '여간 ~지 않다'도 같은 방식으로 써요.

phrases.en: The heat these days is no ordinary heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이만저만'을 명사처럼 쓰고 '아니다'를 붙여 정도가 아주 심하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like a noun plus 'is not', meaning the degree is very high.

phrases.example: 혼자 아이를 키우는 게 이만저만 힘든 게 아니에요.
phrases.en: Raising a child alone is extremely hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 앞에 붙이고 '-(으)ㄴ 게 아니다'로 끝내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before an adjective and ended with '-(으)ㄴ 게 아니다'.

phrases.example: 매일 일찍 일어나는 건 여간 힘들지 않아요.
phrases.en: Getting up early every day is really hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하게 부정문에서만 쓰는 말로, 정도가 매우 심하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar negative-only expression meaning 'very much so'.

explain_en: It almost always appears in negative sentences like '이만저만이 아니다' or '이만저만 ~(으)ㄴ 게 아니다'. A positive sentence like '이만저만 바빠요' sounds odd. Even with the negative ending, the meaning is the opposite: 'extremely intense'. '여간 ~지 않다' works the same way.

examples.en: My mom is very understanding.
I'm lucky to have met such an understanding teacher.
Please be a little more understanding toward your friend.
Thanks to my roommate's understanding, I live comfortably.
If people lack understanding of each other, they fight easily.

examples.ko: 부부 사이에는 서로에 대한 이해심이 필요해요.
examples.en: Between spouses, mutual understanding is needed.

explain: '이해심이 깊다/많다/부족하다'처럼 남의 사정을 헤아리고 받아들이는 마음을 말해요. 내용을 알아듣는 능력인 '이해력'과 달라요. 성격을 칭찬할 때 '이해심이 많은 사람'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 남의 사정에 이해심이 부족해요.
phrases.en: He lacks understanding for other people's situations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 입장을 헤아리지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone can't consider another person's position.

phrases.example: 우리 팀장님은 이해심이 넓어서 실수해도 괜찮아요.
phrases.en: Our team leader is very understanding, so mistakes are okay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 넓고 잘 받아 주는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a broad-minded, accepting person.

phrases.example: 저는 이해심 있는 사람과 결혼하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to marry an understanding person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격을 말할 때 명사를 꾸미는 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form that modifies a noun when describing someone's personality.

explain_en: It is used as '이해심이 깊다/많다/부족하다' for the heart that considers and accepts other people's situations. It differs from '이해력', the ability to grasp content. To praise someone's character, say '이해심이 많은 사람'.

examples.en: I lost all affection for him because he kept breaking promises.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 직원에게 소리치는 걸 보고 정떨어져요.
examples.en: I'm turned off seeing that person yell at staff.
Don't pick only the words that turn people off.

examples.ko: 한 번 정떨어지면 다시 좋아지기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once you're turned off, it's hard to like someone again.

examples.ko: 식당이 너무 더러워서 정떨어져서 다시 안 가요.
examples.en: The restaurant was so dirty I lost all liking for it, so I won't go back.
No wonder you got turned off by that calculating behavior.

explain: '정이 떨어지다'를 줄인 말로 좋아하던 마음이 식어 싫어졌다는 뜻이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 가게나 장소에도 쓰고, 반대는 '정들다'예요.

phrases.en: I went to that shop and lost all affection for it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이지 않은 원래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full, unshortened form.

phrases.en: Please don't say off-putting things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to modify a noun.

phrases.en: His behavior put me off completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 식은 것을 과거형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense expressing that one's affection has cooled.

explain_en: It is the short form of '정이 떨어지다' and means your fondness cooled into dislike. It works for people and also for shops or places, and the opposite is '정들다'.

examples.en: I was so shocked that I wasn't in my right mind.

examples.ko: 제정신이라면 그런 말을 못 할 거예요.
examples.en: No one in their right mind would say that.

examples.ko: 며칠 못 자서 제정신으로 일하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: After days without sleep, it's hard to work with a clear head.

examples.ko: 사고 뒤로 한동안 제정신이 아닌 것처럼 보였어요.
examples.en: After the accident, he seemed out of his mind for a while.
My friend asked if I was out of my mind.
Contacting me at this hour? Are you out of your mind?

explain: '제정신이 아니다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 자주 써요. 놀라거나 화나서 이성을 잃은 상태를 가리켜요. '제정신이야?'는 매우 센 말이라 친하지 않은 사이에서는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그 소식을 듣고 저는 제정신이 아니었어요.
phrases.en: I was out of my mind when I heard the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 화나서 이성을 잃은 상태를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say someone has lost their senses from shock or anger.
phrases.en_equiv: to be out of one's mind

phrases.en: I was shocked, but I soon came to my senses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흥분하거나 놀랐다가 다시 침착해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone calms down after being shocked or upset.

phrases.en: It was a long while before I came to my senses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멍하거나 혼란스럽던 상태에서 정신이 돌아올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one's mind clears after being dazed or confused.

explain_en: It often goes with a negative, as in '제정신이 아니다' (not in one's right mind), describing someone who has lost composure from shock or anger. '제정신이야?' (Are you out of your mind?) is very harsh, so avoid it with people you aren't close to.

examples.en: I'm not joking, I'm serious.

examples.ko: 그 말이 진담인지 농담인지 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I can't tell if that was serious or a joke.

examples.ko: 친구가 웃으면서 한 말에 진담이 섞여 있었어요.
examples.en: My friend's smiling remark had some seriousness mixed in.

examples.ko: 진담으로 들으면 안 돼요, 그냥 장난이에요.
examples.en: Don't take it seriously, it's just a joke.
He had the look of someone speaking seriously.

examples.ko: 선생님은 농담 속에 진담을 담아 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My teacher puts serious points inside her jokes.

explain: '농담'의 반대말이에요. '진담이에요?', '진담으로 들었어요'처럼 말해요. '농담 반 진담 반'은 장난처럼 말했지만 속마음도 들어 있을 때 써요.

phrases.example: 농담 반 진담 반으로 한 말인데 사실 가고 싶어요.
phrases.en: half joking, half serious
phrases.nuance_ko: 장난처럼 말했지만 속마음이 섞여 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said like a joke, but real feeling is mixed in.

explain_en: It is the opposite of 농담. You say 진담이에요? or 진담으로 들었어요. 농담 반 진담 반 means it was said like a joke but contains real feeling.

en: to feel hatred; to feel disgust

examples.en: My older sister recoils at the sight of bugs.
My mother can't stand lies.
I used to hate crowded places.
My friend hates karaoke, so we don't go.
They looked at me with a repelled expression.
The smell was so bad it made people recoil.

explain: '질색하다'는 '싫어하다'와 달리 몸으로 느끼는 거부감이 커요. '질색을 하다'로도 쓰고, 뜻은 거의 같아요. 사람이 주어이고, 싫은 대상은 '을/를'로 받아요.

phrases.en: My friend recoiled in disgust when she saw a cockroach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 싫은 것을 보고 몸으로 거부감을 느꼈다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, meaning one physically recoiled from something disliked.

phrases.en: I am a person who can't stand lies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것을 몹시 싫어하는 사람을 꾸며 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for someone who strongly dislikes something.
phrases.en_equiv: a person who can't stand something

phrases.en: The child avoided the bitter medicine with disgust.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 연결해서 싫어하면서 하는 행동을 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with -며 to describe an action done while showing disgust.

explain_en: Unlike '싫어하다', '질색하다' carries a physical sense of recoiling. '질색을 하다' means almost the same. A person is the subject and the thing disliked takes '을/를'.

examples.en: Tsk, they went without me again.

examples.ko: 쳇, 그 정도는 나도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Humph, I can do that much too.

examples.ko: 동생은 쳇 하고 방으로 들어가 버렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling went 'tsk' and walked into the room.
Tsk, we lost by a hair!

examples.ko: 쳇, 공짜인 줄 알았는데 돈을 내래요.
examples.en: Tsk, I thought it was free, but they say I have to pay.
My friend went 'humph' but helped me in the end.

explain: 쳇은 기분이 안 좋거나 아쉬울 때 혼자 내는 소리예요. 화가 난 것보다는 살짝 삐지거나 못마땅한 느낌이 커요. 친한 사이에서 쓰는 가벼운 소리라서 윗사람에게 쓰면 무례해 보여요.
explain_en: This is a sound people make alone when they feel sulky or let down. It carries more mild sulking or disapproval than real anger. It is casual and used among close people, so using it toward someone older looks rude.

en: to keep silent; to say nothing

examples.en: Everyone stayed silent during the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 질문을 받고 한참 침묵하더니 고개를 저었어요.
examples.en: After the question, he said nothing for a while and then shook his head.
I am angry, so I am not saying anything.

examples.ko: 이럴 때는 침묵하는 게 나을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: In a case like this, saying nothing may be better.
We all ate in silence.
That person will stay silent to the end.

explain: '조용하다'는 소리가 작거나 없는 상태이고, '침묵하다'는 할 말이 있을 수 있는데도 말하지 않는 것이에요. 명사 '침묵'과 함께 '침묵을 지키다', '침묵을 깨다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That person kept silent until the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하지 않고 계속 가만히 있을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for staying quiet and saying nothing.

phrases.en: My friend broke the silence first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하던 분위기에서 처음 말을 꺼낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone speaks first in a quiet moment.

phrases.en: He kept silent about the question.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계속'을 붙여서 오랫동안 말하지 않는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 계속 stresses that someone stays silent for a long time.

explain_en: '조용하다' describes a place or person with little noise; '침묵하다' is choosing not to speak even when there may be something to say. With the noun, the usual pairs are '침묵을 지키다' (keep silent) and '침묵을 깨다' (break the silence).

examples.en: Hehe, actually I ate it first.
My friend giggled sheepishly and said sorry.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 받자 아이가 헤헤 하고 웃었어요.
examples.en: When praised, the child grinned happily.

examples.ko: 헤헤, 이거 제가 직접 만든 거예요!
examples.en: Hehe, I made this myself!
I was sleepy and just kept giggling.
My younger sibling ran off to the room giggling.

explain: 헤헤는 쑥스럽거나 기분이 좋아서 장난스럽게 웃는 소리예요. '하하'는 시원하게 크게 웃을 때, '히히'는 장난스럽게 웃을 때, 헤헤는 조금 멋쩍을 때 써요. 문자나 채팅에서 많이 쓰고 격식 있는 글에는 안 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling ran away giggling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤헤보다 더 장난스럽게 웃을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a more playful laugh than 헤헤.

phrases.en: My friend laughed out loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤헤보다 시원하고 크게 웃을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a bigger, hearty laugh compared to 헤헤.

phrases.en: I got praised and laughed bashfully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헤헤'를 한 번 더 이어 붙여 웃음이 계속되는 쑥스럽고 기쁜 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating 헤헤 once more gives a continuing, shy and happy laugh.

explain_en: 헤헤 is a playful laugh when you feel shy or pleased. '하하' is a hearty laugh and '히히' a mischievous one, while 헤헤 fits a slightly sheepish moment. It is common in texts and chats but not in formal writing.

en: to cheer; to shout for joy

examples.en: When the goal went in, the crowd cheered all at once.
At the news of passing, the whole family shouted with joy.
You can hear the fans cheering all the way outside.

examples.ko: 아이들은 눈이 온다는 말에 환호하며 뛰어나갔어요.
examples.en: The kids cheered and ran outside at the news that it was snowing.
The people who were cheering suddenly went quiet.
I was surprised when the audience cheered as I greeted them on stage.

explain: 환호하다는 기쁨이나 감격으로 큰 소리를 지르며 반길 때 써요. 많은 사람이 함께 있는 상황에서 자주 쓰고, 혼자 기뻐하는 모습은 '좋아하다', '기뻐하다'로 말해요. '환호성', '환호를 보내다'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Cheers burst out when the game ended.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기뻐서 지르는 큰 소리를 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for the loud shout of joy.

phrases.en: The audience sent cheers to the players.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가에게 기쁜 마음으로 박수와 소리를 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving joyful cheers to someone.

phrases.en: The children were happy to get the present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 지르지 않아도 되고, 혼자 기뻐할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Doesn't need shouting and works when one is happy alone.

explain_en: It means shouting out loud to welcome something with joy or deep feeling. It fits scenes with many people together, while one person's happiness is usually 좋아하다 or 기뻐하다. It also appears as nouns, as in 환호성 and 환호를 보내다.
